resources.string: OpenBlur finds the faces in a video. You choose which ones to blur, and it saves a blurred copy. The original video is not changed.
OpenBlur has no network permission, so it cannot upload your videos.
No scanned videos yet. After you choose a video and the scan finishes, it appears here, and you can open it again without another scan.
Your scanned videos could not be loaded.
That scan could not be opened. The video may have been moved or deleted. Choose the video again to scan it.
OpenBlur closed before your last save finished, so that video was not saved. You can save it again from its scan.
The scan could not be deleted.
This phone has no app for choosing a video. Open the video in a file manager or gallery app and share it to OpenBlur.
OpenBlur is still working on another video, so the new one was not opened. Finish or cancel the current video first.
The scan of %1$s and your blur choices for it will be deleted. The video itself stays on your phone.
Keep this screen open. The scan can stop if you switch to another app.
The scan so far will be discarded.
OpenBlur found no video it can read in this file. The file may be damaged, or in a format this phone does not support. Try another video.
This phone could not decode the video
The phone\'s video decoder stopped while reading the file. Close other apps that use the camera or play video, then scan again.
The face detector could not start
The face detection model inside the app failed to load or run. Close OpenBlur, open it again and scan again. If this keeps happening, reinstall the app.
The phone ran out of memory
Close other apps, then scan again.
The scan could not be saved
Free some storage space on this phone, then scan again.
Scan again. If it stops at the same point, the file may be damaged.
Checking what this phone can encode
OpenBlur could not check this phone\'s video encoders.
This phone cannot encode this video
No video encoder on this phone accepts this video\'s size and format, so OpenBlur cannot save a blurred copy here.
What will differ from the original
Uses a bitrate a little above the original.
Uses about twice the original bitrate. The file is larger.
The original records where it was filmed. Turn this on to leave that out of the copy.
Nothing is set to blur. The copy would show everything the original shows.
The copy is saved to this phone\'s video library as %1$s. The original is not changed.
OpenBlur could not prepare the blur for this video. Close this sheet and open it again.
On this version of Android, OpenBlur needs the storage permission to save the copy. Allow it when asked, or in the app\'s settings, then save again.
The export did not start. Save again.
No face or area is set to blur, so the saved video will show everything the original shows.
The copy uses the H.264 codec, because this phone cannot encode the original\'s codec at this size.
The copy uses the HEVC codec, because this phone cannot encode the original\'s codec at this size.
The original is HDR. The copy is standard dynamic range, because this phone cannot encode this HDR format. Bright areas and colours can look different.
The original\'s Dolby Vision data is left out of the copy.
The original has 10-bit colour. The copy has 8-bit colour, which can show banding in smooth areas such as sky.
The original has more than one audio track. The copy keeps only the first.
The audio is encoded again instead of copied, so it is not identical to the original\'s audio.
This phone\'s encoder may save a picture size that differs from the original.
The bitrate is limited to the highest value this phone\'s encoder accepts.
This phone\'s encoder does not state that it can keep up with this size and frame rate. Saving can take longer than the video lasts.
You can switch to other apps. The export keeps running.
The part of the video encoded so far will be discarded. Your blur choices are kept.
The saved video cannot be played here. Open it in another app to check it.
The export reported no differences from the original. The table above shows what was read back from the saved file.
No app on this phone can open this video.
Details copied. Paste them into a bug report.
No video was saved. Your blur choices are still in the editor.
This phone has no video encoder that can save this video.
No setting in OpenBlur changes this. A different phone may be able to export the video.
The original video could not be read.
Check that the video is still on this phone and has not been moved or deleted, then export again.
This phone\'s video decoder stopped during the export.
Close other apps that use the camera or play video, then export again.
This phone\'s video encoder stopped during the export.
Close other apps that use the camera or record video, then export again.
The phone ran out of storage space.
Free some space, then export again. The save sheet shows the estimated file size.
The finished video could not be written to this phone\'s video library.
Check that storage is available and that OpenBlur is allowed to save files, then export again.
Android stopped the export because it ran longer than the system allows in the background.
Export again and keep OpenBlur open on the screen until it finishes.
The export stopped for a reason OpenBlur does not recognise.
Export again. If it stops again, copy the details and report them on the source code page listed in About.

Your video is scanned, blurred and saved on this phone. OpenBlur cannot use the network, because it does not ask for the network permission. You can check this yourself: open the app info screen and look at the permissions.
Scans are kept on this phone until you delete them from the list on the first screen.
The app info screen could not be opened. Look for OpenBlur under Apps in the phone\'s settings.
